design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (patient_payment_plans, category payplan).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {"key": "env_0032_physical_therapy_clinic_network/patient_payment_plans/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 5]}. Root payplan_ext_past_due_catch_up takes 6 factors; prerequisite payplan_ext_missed_installment_late_fee takes 5. --tasks 2 shows task 1 drawing 1 prerequisite and [4, 5]; task 1 is reserved the term-modification line (patient-accepted modified installment) with a returned-payment-fee prerequisite, none of which task 0 touches.

[Why this is a good test] The caller asks only to "get caught up". To pay the right figure the agent must (a) read the catch-up policy and notice its prerequisite sentence ("The catch-up amount is fixed only after the installment most recently recorded as missed carries its late-fee entry on the plan."), (b) see in the ledger that the 2026-09-01 missed installment has no late-fee entry (the only late fee is for 2025-09-01), (c) work out from the late-fee policy that its write is the one that books that entry, compute the fee through five factors, book it, and only then (d) compute the catch-up through six factors over the plan ledger, the plan-of-care ledger and the hardship case, and hand the payment to the patient. Difficulty is reading policy, reconciling a 41-row plan ledger, and arithmetic, not tool guessing: only one tool books late fees and only one takes catch-up payments.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before: nothing (task 0). Claimed: payplan_ext_missed_installment_late_fee (state_due, assess_payment_plan_late_fee_b662389f, agent) and payplan_ext_past_due_catch_up (on_request, pay_payment_plan_past_due_400c78cb, user). Headroom for task 1: payplan_terms_modified (modification), returned-payment fee booking, add-ons, holidays and adjustments all remain unclaimed.

[Problem-tree card] Root payplan_ext_past_due_catch_up <- payplan_ext_missed_installment_late_fee. Edge kind value_input, gate c_late_fees, form state, policy_source "The catch-up amount is fixed only after the installment most recently recorded as missed carries its late-fee entry on the plan." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; the waited-on side is a record-visible state (a late-fee entry carrying the latest missed installment's due date); no tool, id or code token; scope exactly the latest missed installment, matching the late-fee rule which books one entry for "the installment most recently recorded as missed". Exactly one write of this difficulty books a late-fee entry (assess_payment_plan_late_fee_b662389f); the catch-up and every other tool write no fee rows, so the state singles out that write. Derivation: sentence + ledger (missed 2026-09-01 at payment_plan_events MISSED26, late fee only on 2025-09-01 at LATE25) + late-fee rule ("A late-fee entry is booked once for the installment most recently recorded as missed on the plan; it carries that installment's due date and adds its amount to the plan balance.") -> book the late fee first. Direction: affirmative "only after", the way a billing desk states that a payoff-type figure rests on complete charges. Opening falsity: no row with event_type payplan_fee_assessed, fee_kind late_fee, installment_due_date 2026-09-01. Resolving action owner agent; root owner user. Order late fee -> catch-up; single edge, no parallel branch. Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): without the late-fee write the catch-up is 232.42 instead of 234.04 and the fee row is missing. user_scenario names no fee and no preliminary step; tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

[Base-invariant card] Late-fee write subject payplan_fee_assessed: governing base policy payplan_evt_delinquency, no structured eligibility (policy_scope); its rule "Each missed installment adds late_fee, up to late_fees_max_per_plan late fees in the plan's life" is superseded clause-by-clause by the extended late-fee step (declared in overwrite); "the first late fee is waived on request" stays in force (not requested on this call). Catch-up subjects payplan_payment_received + payplan_cured: payplan_evt_payments gate payable_status ("Payments are accepted only on a plan in active, past_due or defaulted status.") satisfied by payment_plans.status = past_due on the target agreement (correlation key payment_plan_id); payplan_evt_delinquency policy_scope; its whole cure sentence ("A past-due plan becomes current when every missed installment is paid in full where cure_requires_full_past_due is true, or when the latest missed installment is paid where it is false.") is superseded (declared) by "A past-due plan is current again when its catch-up amount is paid in one payment, the extra-principal credit standing for the part of the missed installments it covers, whatever the tier's cure_requires_full_past_due.", because the catch-up clears the whole current delinquency and its credit can stand for part of an installment. From payplan_evt_payments two clauses are superseded (declared): "where autopay_required is true installments are collected automatically and manual payments are extra." (the hand-taken catch-up counts as an installment payment) and the extra-principal clause (pre-delinquency extra principal on tiers that do not shorten the term). No time gate applies to either subject.

[Business-object card] Target object: agreement PP (Large-Balance 18-Month, signed 2025-06-04, installment 149.35). Current delinquency = entries fewer than 1 whole month before 2026-09-29, because the latest automatic collection was the installment due 2026-08-01: rows included are missed 2026-09-01, returned fee 25.00 (2026-09-01), late fee booked by the prerequisite, installment payment 60.00 (2026-09-16), extra principal 25.00 (2026-09-21). Rows excluded: the 2025-09-01 delinquency (failed drafts, 25.00 returned fee, 10.00 late fee, 184.35 catch-up on 2025-09-19), twelve automatic collections, the down payment, fourteen enrollment transfers. Settled objects: the 2025-09-01 installment and its fees were paid by the 2025-09-19 payment.

[Factor card - late fee, 5 factors, Step 5 run] late_fee_count_window (method): age 15 months, 1 missed within 12 months -> count late fees within 12 months = 0; baseline whole life = 1 -> result 5.76. late_fee_step (parameter): count 0 -> first_late_fee 7.50; baseline late_fee 10.00 -> 5.76. draft_lapse_share (parameter, multi-source): insufficient_funds and 11 automatic collections within 12 months -> 0.8; baseline 1.0 -> 5.40. payment_effort_share (parameter): 60.00 paid against the installment -> 0.9; baseline 1.0 -> 4.80. active_treatment_share (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty plan): 4 visits on the active low-back plan of care within 1 month, 0 statements within 6 months -> 0.8; baseline 1.0 -> 5.40. Result RND(7.50 x 0.8 x 0.9 x 0.8, 2) = 4.32; whole baseline 10.00. Near-miss: the 2025-09-01 late fee is exactly 12 whole months back (MONTHS(2025-09-01, 2026-09-29) = 12) and falls outside the 12-month window; a reader who counts it gets the 10.00 step. Near-miss 2: the 2026-08-24 evaluation visit is 1 whole month back and does not count toward the treatment window, but four September visits do.

[Factor card - catch-up, 6 factors, Step 5 run on the world after the late fee] late_fee_collection_share 0.5 (1 missed in 12 months, 11 collections) baseline -> 235.66; returned_fee_collection_share 0.6 (15-month-old plan, 1 returned fee in 12 months) -> 241.54; extra_principal_credit (method) credits the 25.00 extra principal of 2026-09-21 -> baseline 259.04; next_installment_pull 1.0 (28 days >= 25 since 2026-09-01, returned fee on it) -> baseline 84.69; repeat_delinquency_principal_share 0.05 (earlier miss outside 12 months) -> baseline 226.57; assistance_share 0.75 (hardship application pending since 2026-09-18, cross-category hardship) -> baseline 238.33. Result 234.04; whole baseline 118.67. Multi-source factors of the task: draft_lapse_share, active_treatment_share and five of the catch-up's factors; cross-category factors: active_treatment_share (plan, the other difficulty's product) and assistance_share (hardship). Stamps: no field names any factor outcome; the hardship tier name is the level applied for, not the decision.

[Seed design] Customer row; two Commercial PPO plans of care (closed 2025 shoulder episode whose 14 charges were enrolled, with visits, charges and transfer adjustments; active 2026 low-back episode with 5 billed visits and no charges yet because explanations of benefits are pending); one Large-Balance plan with 41 ledger rows; one pending hardship case. Removing the September 2026 visits flips the treatment share to 1.0 (late fee 5.40, catch-up moves); removing the 2025 late fee row flips the count window to equal counts (step still 7.50 but the window factor's baseline then equals gold - so that row is load-bearing); removing the pending hardship case flips the assistance share; removing the 60.00 or 25.00 payments moves both results. Automatic clauses checked: the plan has 1 consecutive missed installment (default notice needs 3), so no default notice is owed; no add-on, holiday or reinstatement is pending; the closed plan of care has a zero balance; the pending hardship case owes no discount yet.

[Persona design] Lorraine Pettigrew, polite and slightly embarrassed, opens with the returned September payment and the wish to get caught up today; identity details only when asked (phone to locate, then DOB and ZIP, account number as a spare); the 60.00 and 25.00 portal payments, the weekly back therapy, the pending assistance application and her keeping the autopay account are given only when asked; she agrees to a preliminary posting if told one is needed, pays the quoted amount by card when handed the payment, declines any other change, and closes once the plan is current. She never names a figure or a fee.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(DOB, ZIP) -> find_payment_plans -> find_payment_plan_events -> find_care_plans -> find_care_plan_events -> find_hardship_cases -> unlock + call assess_payment_plan_late_fee_b662389f(PP, 2026-09-01, 4.32) -> unlock_user + (patient) pay_payment_plan_past_due_400c78cb(PP, 2026-09-01, 234.04, card). Terminal: two new ledger rows, plan_balance 686.63 + 4.32 - 234.04 = 456.91, status active.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] Using only the published rules, the tool schemas, the lookups and the persona: the plan is past due; the catch-up rule's prerequisite sentence sends the reader to the late-fee rule; the ledger yields the late fee 4.32 and then the catch-up 234.04 exactly as gold; the payment method comes from the persona ('card').

[Places most easily got wrong] Counting the 2025-09-01 late fee (exactly 12 months back) and charging the 10.00 step; skipping the late fee and quoting 232.42; forgetting the 25.00 extra principal of 2026-09-21 (it carries no installment due date, so a reader who filters payments by the missed installment misses it) and quoting 259.04; leaving out the coming installment (84.69); applying the shares to rounded intermediate amounts instead of rounding once. The next-installment pull collects the 2026-10-01 installment amount with the catch-up because the account that funds the 2026-10-01 draft has just bounced; the rule fixes this, and the persona never pushes either way.

[Verification runs] Scratch evaluator (check_compute.build_env/eval_compute on the seeded world, then on the world with the late fee replayed through the real tool): late fee result 4.32, factor baselines 5.76/5.76/5.40/4.80/5.40, whole baseline 10.00; catch-up result 234.04, factor baselines 235.66/241.54/259.04/84.69/226.57/238.33, whole baseline 118.67; catch-up without the late-fee write 232.42. Per-task gates for --task 0: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (11 actions, closure 93 = initial 93), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK (2 computations, 11 factors, 2 cross-difficulty), GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[Revisions] (1) check_extended counted a private helper in task_tools.py as an unnamed task tool -> helper inlined into each tool -> EXTENDED OK. (2) Late-fee step ordering would have charged first_late_fee on a tier whose late_fees_max_per_plan is 0 -> cap tier placed first and the first-fee tier conditioned on a cap above zero, in the rule, the overwrite quotation and compute together. (3) Plan-of-care deductible_remaining on the closed shoulder plan was 0.00 while 3000.00 of deductible charges posted -> set to 3000.00 at the 2025-02-20 verification; no computation reads it.

[Revisions round 2 - policy audit] F1 does not concern this task. O1: the base clause 'where autopay_required is true installments are collected automatically and manual payments are extra.' is now declared superseded by the rule sentence 'The catch-up payment is taken by hand and counts as an installment payment toward the missed installments, never as an extra payment, even on a tier whose installments are otherwise collected automatically.' O2: the cure overwrite now supersedes the whole base cure sentence and is replaced by a cure sentence ('A past-due plan is current again when its catch-up amount is paid in one payment, the extra-principal credit standing for the part of the missed installments it covers, whatever the tier's cure_requires_full_past_due.') instead of the amount sentence. O4 (charter-wide): 'most recently recorded as missed' is now read by the day the missed entry was recorded (LATEST without the due-date ordering), which picks the same 2026-09-01 entry here; the edge condition says 'with the latest event_date'. O7: the factor goodwill_principal_share is renamed repeat_delinquency_principal_share (params repeat_share_recent / repeat_share_older), since it adds principal rather than conceding anything. O8: pull_share_card renamed pull_share_unreturned and the rule now states how the pulled amount is applied: 'The pulled amount, being above what the missed installments call for, is applied by overpayment_handling like any other amount above what is due, and the coming installment is still collected on its own due date.' Proof text: the cross-category factor list now names assistance_share. No scored value moved: late fee 4.32, catch-up 234.04, all factor baselines and baseline_result unchanged on re-run.
user_scenario:
You are Lorraine Pettigrew, 64, a part-time school office assistant in Wilmington, North Carolina. You are polite, a little embarrassed about money, and you like to have things settled before you hang up. You keep the email the clinic sent you open while you talk.

You are calling because an email from Piedmont Motion Physical Therapy told you that your patient payment plan is past due because your bank sent back the automatic payment for September. You want to get caught up on the payment plan today, over the phone, so the plan is back in good standing. You open with something like: "Hi, I got an email that my payment plan with you is past due because my bank returned the September payment, and I'd like to get caught up today." You do not know how much that takes; you expect the representative to look it up and tell you, and you never name a figure yourself.

To find your account you give the phone number on file, 9105554418. Only when the representative asks you to confirm who you are do you give your date of birth, July 23, 1962 (1962-07-23), and your ZIP code, 28409; if they ask for something more you can read the account number off your statement, PM-3406152.

There are a few things you mention only if the representative asks about them. You already paid $60 through the patient portal on September 16, and on September 21 you put another $25 through the portal on a screen that said something about principal, because that was all you could spare that week. You are still coming in once a week for your lower back at the Oleander Drive clinic. On September 18 you applied for the clinic's financial assistance program and sent in your pay stubs, and you have not heard back yet. Your September problem was simply that your checking account was short when the payment was drawn; you are keeping the automatic payment on that same account. You have no other payment plan and no other bills you want to talk about on this call.

As the call goes on, if the representative explains that something has to be put on your payment plan before the catch-up amount can be worked out, you say that is fine and they can go ahead. When the representative tells you the amount needed to get caught up and hands you the payment to make yourself, you pay that exact amount on the call with your Visa debit card (the card option), recorded against the September installment exactly as they tell you, and you then read back the confirmation and new balance you see. If the representative offers to change anything else on the plan, you politely say you only want to get caught up today. Once the payment has gone through and the plan is shown as current again, you thank them and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain of one edge: the catch-up depends on the late fee and nothing depends on the catch-up, so the only topological order is late fee then catch-up.
